dataBackup.title: Backup & Restore
dataBackup.intro: Save categories, phrases, images, and settings to a file on this device, or restore from a previous backup. Nothing is uploaded to the cloud.
dataBackup.exportHint: Downloads a JSON file you can store in Files, iCloud Drive, or email to yourself.
dataBackup.importHint: Replaces all local categories, phrases, images, and settings with the backup file.
dataBackup.importWarning: This will overwrite everything on this device. Export a backup first if you want to keep the current data.

onboarding.welcomeP1: Switch2GO is an Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) app designed for people with Cerebral Visual Impairment (CVI) and others who need accessible communication.
onboarding.welcomeP2: Choose phrases organized into categories, then tap or select them to speak out loud. The app works with touch, eye gaze, head tracking, and keyboard switches — use whatever works best.
onboarding.welcomeP3: The interface uses high-contrast, customizable layouts with fewer symbols per page to reduce visual complexity. Every phrase can be individually styled with custom colors, images, borders, and text sizes.
onboarding.orientationP1: For eye and head tracking, use landscape orientation with the front camera facing you. Tracking may pause in portrait or when the camera cannot see your face.
onboarding.orientationP2: If tracking seems off, rotate to landscape, allow camera access when prompted, and hold the device steady for a moment so tracking can recover.
onboarding.orientationP3: Touch and keyboard selection (keys 1–4) work in any orientation.
onboarding.navigationP1: The main screen shows category tiles. Tap a category to see its phrases, then tap a phrase to speak it out loud. Use the back control to return to categories.
onboarding.navigationP2: Eye Gaze mode: keep your head as still as possible and move only your eyes. Look at a button and hold your gaze until the dwell ring completes to select it.
onboarding.navigationP3: Head Tracking mode: move your head in the direction you want the cursor to go.
onboarding.navigationP4: In both tracking modes, the pointer shows the current location and the green progress ring fills while you dwell.
onboarding.navigationP5: To change your input method, open Settings and go to Selection Mode. You can choose Touch Only, Head Tracking, or Eye Gaze.
onboarding.navigationP6: You can add, edit, reorder, and delete categories and phrases from Settings → Edit Categories & Phrases.
onboarding.imageToolP1: When editing a phrase's image, you can open the Image Tool on our support website — it helps you find and prepare the perfect picture for any phrase.
onboarding.imageToolP2: Search Wikimedia Commons for thousands of free images — real photographs, not abstract icons — which are much better for users with CVI.
onboarding.imageToolP3: The tool can automatically remove the background from any image, isolating just the subject.
onboarding.imageToolP4: You can also add a high-contrast colored outline around the object. Once you're happy with the result, download the image and assign it to your phrase.
onboarding.cviFriendlyP1: For users with Cortical Visual Impairment (CVI), how a phrase looks matters as much as what it says.
onboarding.cviFriendlyP2: Use a BLACK background — dark backgrounds reduce visual clutter and help the foreground content stand out.
onboarding.cviFriendlyP3: Use RED or YELLOW text — these high-contrast colors are typically the easiest for CVI users to see.
onboarding.cviFriendlyP4: Use REAL photographic images, not cartoon icons or abstract symbols.
onboarding.cviFriendlyP5: Keep it simple — show fewer symbols per page (2–4 is ideal). Go to Settings → CVI Display.
onboarding.cviDisplayP1: Control how many phrase symbols appear on each page. Fewer symbols means less visual clutter — choose between 2, 3, or 4 symbols per page.
onboarding.cviDisplayP2: Assign a specific background color to each symbol position. Consistent position colors help users learn where to look.
onboarding.cviDisplayP3: Find these settings at: Settings → CVI Display and Categories Display.
onboarding.switchP1: On the web app, press keys 1–4 on your keyboard to select the corresponding phrase on the current page (left-to-right, top-to-bottom).
onboarding.switchP2: Touch, eye gaze, and head tracking continue to work alongside keyboard selection.
onboarding.switchP3: USB adaptive switches are not supported in the browser version; use the iPad app for hardware switch control.
onboarding.privacyP1: This app is designed with privacy as a core principle. We do not collect, store, or transmit any personal information from your device.
onboarding.privacyP2: We collect ZERO information. No analytics, crash reports, cloud sync, cookies, or transmission of camera or microphone data.
onboarding.privacyP3: No camera images, video, or eye tracking data is stored or transmitted. All processing happens locally in your browser.
onboarding.privacyP4: We share NO data with anyone. No third-party analytics, advertising, or cloud services.
onboarding.privacyP5: This app is safe for children and students of all ages. No data collection means compliance with COPPA, FERPA, and GDPR.
onboarding.privacyP6: Our support website also lets you create custom phrase images with background removal and colored outlines — great for CVI-friendly symbols.

troubleshootingGuide.intro: Having trouble? Check the sections below for common issues and solutions.
troubleshootingGuide.modes1: Open Settings from the gear icon on the home screen.
troubleshootingGuide.modes3: Choose Touch Only, Head Tracking, or Eye Gaze Tracking.
troubleshootingGuide.modes4: The change takes effect when you return to categories or phrases.
troubleshootingGuide.modes5: You can switch between modes at any time — the app remembers your last choice.
troubleshootingGuide.orientation1: Eye and head tracking work best in landscape with the front camera facing you.
troubleshootingGuide.orientation2: Allow camera access when the browser prompts you. If you denied it, enable the camera in site settings.
troubleshootingGuide.orientation3: If tracking pauses, rotate to landscape and ensure your face is visible to the camera.
troubleshootingGuide.orientation4: Touch and keyboard keys 1–4 still work when tracking is unavailable.
troubleshootingGuide.tracking1: Make sure your face is clearly visible to the front camera — avoid covering your face or wearing reflective glasses.
troubleshootingGuide.tracking2: Ensure you have good, even lighting. Avoid backlighting (bright light behind you).
troubleshootingGuide.tracking3: Check that the browser has permission to use the camera for this site.
troubleshootingGuide.tracking4: Try the Recenter Cursor button at the top of Settings if the pointer seems offset.
troubleshootingGuide.tracking5: If tracking was working before but stopped, refresh the page or close and reopen the tab.
troubleshootingGuide.tracking6: For eye gaze, sit at a comfortable distance from the screen (roughly 40–60 cm / 16–24 inches).
troubleshootingGuide.switch1: On the phrases screen, press keys 1, 2, 3, or 4 to speak the phrase in that position on the current page.
troubleshootingGuide.switch2: Order is left-to-right, top-to-bottom, matching the on-screen layout.
troubleshootingGuide.switch3: USB adaptive switches require the iPad app; they are not available in the web browser.
troubleshootingGuide.safariIntro: Use this quick checklist when testing on iPad in Safari (or Add to Home Screen). All processing stays on the device.
troubleshootingGuide.safariEye: Eye gaze: landscape, face visible, dwell ring completes on a phrase.
troubleshootingGuide.safariHead: Head tracking: pointer follows head movement; double-blink recenters when enabled.
troubleshootingGuide.safariDwell: Dwell: green ring fills at Timing & Sensitivity dwell time; repeat dwell works if enabled.
troubleshootingGuide.safariCameraDeny: Camera denied: app falls back to touch; re-enable camera in Settings → Safari → Camera for this site.
troubleshootingGuide.safariTouch: Touch and keys 1–4 always work when tracking is off.
